titleZh: 價格高得令人負擔不起

target.pattern: (?:\bpric(?:e|es|ed|ing) (?:train travel |the tickets |the classes |them |it )?out of (?:people[’']s|our|their|my|many families[’']) reach\b)|(?:\bpriced out of higher education\b)

brief.meaningEn: Make an activity or product unaffordable for the people concerned by setting or raising its price.
brief.meaningZh: 因定價或加價，令有關人士負擔不起活動或產品。
brief.grammar: be priced out of an activity or institution, including higher education, when costs prevent access; also price classes or tickets out of someone’s reach.
brief.register: Contextual combination of price and the conventional out-of-reach metaphor; do not present the whole supplied wording as a separate dictionary idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 是價格造成負擔障礙，不等於物理距離遠、不感興趣或所有人都買不起。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要指明受影響人士與負擔情況，不能只憑價格上升就判所有人無法參與。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把價格變動連到具體參與障礙，保留誰仍能負擔的區別。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: If fares rise again, train travel may be priced out of people's reach.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 145, row 8; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: No qualified student should be priced out of higher education.

listening.en: The new ticket price has put the concerts beyond our budget; they have been priced out of our reach, although we still want to attend.
listening.zh: 新票價超出我們預算；音樂會價格已高得我們負擔不起，雖然我們仍想去。
listening.promptZh: 說話者沒有去的原因是甚麼？

options.en: The group cannot afford the new price despite remaining interested.
options.zh: 小組仍有興趣，卻負擔不起新價。

options.en: The group can afford the price but has lost interest in the music.
options.zh: 小組負擔得起，卻對音樂失去興趣。

options.en: The concerts have moved to a venue the group cannot travel to.
options.zh: 音樂會搬到小組無法前往的場地。

options.en: The group bought tickets before the increase and no longer needs a booking.
options.zh: 小組加價前已買票，不再需預訂。

listening.explanationZh: beyond our budget 及 still want 明確分開負擔與興趣，沒有搬場或已買票資料。

reply.promptZh: 你們為甚麼沒有訂這次音樂會？
reply.promptEn: Why have you not booked this concert?

options.en: The new price is more than our budget allows.
options.zh: 新價格超出我們預算。

options.en: The tickets have been priced out of our reach.
options.zh: 票價已高得我們負擔不起。

options.en: We still like the concerts, but cannot afford the new tickets.
options.zh: 我們仍喜歡音樂會，卻負擔不起新票價。

options.en: The cost prevents us from booking this time.
options.zh: 費用令我們這次無法預訂。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以費用解釋未訂票；金句的 reach 指負擔能力。

scene.promptZh: 課程由低收費變成你們負擔不起的價錢，內容及地點沒變，你們仍想學。哪句準確？

options.en: The location, rather than the fee, now prevents us from attending.
options.zh: 現在阻止我們上課的是地點，不是費用。

options.en: The classes have been priced out of our reach.
options.zh: 課程價格已高得我們負擔不起。

options.en: Our interest ended before the fee changed.
options.zh: 收費改變前，我們已失去興趣。

scene.explanationZh: 題目給價格超出能力，而非地點或興趣變化。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以說課程已 priced out of their reach？

options.en: The new fee exceeds what those families can afford.
options.zh: 新收費超過那些家庭負擔能力。

options.en: The families cannot join because of the revised fee.
options.zh: 家庭因新收費無法參與。

options.en: The fee rose slightly, but those families can still comfortably afford it.
options.zh: 收費略升，但那些家庭仍能輕鬆負擔。

contrast.explanationZh: 加價本身不等於負擔不起，須看有關人士的情況。

dialogue.promptZh: 主辦者把未報名都歸因沒興趣，但已收到有意參加家庭表示負擔不起的回覆。哪句應對較準確？

options.en: The fee may have priced the classes out of their reach; record that cost barrier separately from a lack of interest.
options.zh: 費用可能令這些課程超出他們的負擔能力；應把這項費用障礙與沒興趣分開記錄。

options.en: Treat willingness to attend as evidence that every family can afford the fee.
options.zh: 把願意參加當每個家庭都負擔得起的證據。

options.en: Use the number of empty places alone to describe families’ interest.
options.zh: 只按空缺名額描述家庭興趣。

dialogue.explanationZh: 回覆已提供負擔障礙，不可把空缺直接等同沒興趣。

speaking.en: The tickets have been priced out of our reach, even though we still value the performances.
speaking.zh: 票價已高得我們負擔不起，即使我們仍珍惜演出。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把費用障礙與欣賞程度分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你的攝影小組想買一件共享器材，新款報價超出合資上限，但現有器材仍可借用。用一至兩句英文說明負擔限制及替代安排，不評論品質。
writing.selfCheckZh: 說明新器材超出合資上限及仍可借舊器材，不把負擔不起當品質差或沒有興趣。

examples.en: The new equipment has been priced out of our reach, so we will keep borrowing the existing kit for now.
examples.zh: 新器材價格已高得我們負擔不起，所以暫時繼續借現有套裝。

examples.en: The price increase has priced it out of our reach; borrowing the shared kit remains an option for the group.
examples.zh: 加價令它變得我們負擔不起；小組仍可選借共享套裝。

takeaways.en: The revised fee has priced the classes out of many families’ reach.
takeaways.zh: 新收費令課程變得許多家庭負擔不起。

takeaways.en: Rising tuition can leave capable applicants priced out of higher education.
takeaways.zh: 學費上漲可能令有能力的申請者負擔不起高等教育。

titleZh: 作品默默掛着卻未引發交流

target.pattern: \bhang(?:s|ing)? there in silence\b|\bhung there in silence\b

brief.meaningEn: In this art metaphor, remain displayed without helping viewers engage with the work’s meaning.
brief.meaningZh: 在這個藝術比喻中，作品雖展示着，卻未讓觀者接觸它的意義。
brief.grammar: a painting hangs/hung there in silence; can/would hang there in silence. Silence personifies a work as not communicating.
brief.register: Contextual personification, not a fixed idiom or a rule that paintings must have sound.
brief.boundaryZh: 不只指展廳沒聲音，也不表示畫沒有價值；安靜觀看本身仍可很投入。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需有缺少理解或交流的情境，不能因沒導賞或沒聲響就斷言觀者不理解。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述展示與觀者理解之間的落差，不貶低安靜欣賞。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A label alone can make a striking painting hang there in silence.

listening.en: Without any account of the unfamiliar symbols, the painting seemed to hang there in silence for these visitors: they looked briefly but could not connect its details to a story.
listening.zh: 沒有陌生符號的解說，這幅畫對這些訪客彷彿只默默掛着：他們看了一會，卻無法把細節連成故事。
listening.promptZh: silence 在此重點是甚麼？

options.en: The visitors had not found a way into the meaning of the displayed details.
options.zh: 訪客尚未找到理解展示細節意義的途徑。

options.en: The visitors studied the symbols deeply and formed a detailed interpretation.
options.zh: 訪客深入研究符號，形成詳細解讀。

options.en: The gallery was closed, so nobody could see the painting.
options.zh: 畫廊關閉，所以沒人能看畫。

options.en: The work had been removed after visitors asked questions.
options.zh: 訪客提問後，作品已移走。

listening.explanationZh: 作品在場但訪客無法連結細節，才支持不交流的比喻；不是關閉或已移走。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼想為這幅陌生符號畫加背景資料？
reply.promptEn: Why do you want background information beside this unfamiliar symbolic painting?

options.en: These visitors need a way to connect its details with the artist’s story.
options.zh: 這些訪客需要把細節與畫家故事連起來的途徑。

options.en: For these visitors, it seems to hang there in silence without that context.
options.zh: 對這些訪客而言，沒背景時它彷彿只默默掛着。

options.en: People are seeing the picture without understanding what the symbols refer to.
options.zh: 大家看見畫，卻不懂符號所指。

options.en: Some clear context could help viewers engage with what they are looking at.
options.zh: 清楚背景可幫觀者理解正在看的內容。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明理解入口不足，金句不是要求在畫旁播放聲響。

scene.promptZh: 畫作一直展出，這批初訪者卻不知道其中人物及事件關係，只匆匆走過。策展人想描述尚未與觀者交流的作品。哪句貼切？

options.en: The painting seems to hang there in silence for these viewers.
options.zh: 對這些觀者而言，畫彷彿只默默掛着。

options.en: The viewers have already connected every figure to the event.
options.zh: 觀者已把每個人物與事件連起來。

options.en: The painting is no longer on display for visitors to see.
options.zh: 畫已不再展示給訪客看。

scene.explanationZh: 展示與理解不同，題目明示尚未理解而非移走。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持這個不交流的畫作比喻？

options.en: Visitors see the object but cannot relate its unexplained details to any context.
options.zh: 訪客看見物件，卻無法把未解說細節連到背景。

options.en: Visitors quietly study the details and explain a thoughtful interpretation.
options.zh: 訪客安靜研究細節，並說出深思過的解讀。

options.en: A brief glance ends without viewers finding meaning in the unfamiliar imagery.
options.zh: 觀者簡短看過，尚未在陌生意象中找到意思。

contrast.explanationZh: 安靜仍可有深入理解，不能只按聲音判斷是否交流。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴以為展廳安靜就表示所有畫都沒有與人交流，想單加大聲音效。哪句建議最好？

options.en: Check what viewers understand before deciding what context or support would help.
options.zh: 先查觀者理解甚麼，再決定有何背景或支援有幫助。

options.en: Use room volume as the only measure of engagement with the paintings.
options.zh: 只用展廳聲量量度觀者投入。

options.en: Add louder effects before finding out which details visitors cannot interpret.
options.zh: 未查訪客不懂哪些細節，就加更大聲音效。

dialogue.explanationZh: 比喻關乎理解與投入，不是聲量越大越好。

speaking.en: Without that context, the painting seemed to hang there in silence for the new visitors.
speaking.zh: 沒有那背景時，畫對初訪者彷彿只默默掛着。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再描述這批觀者未找到理解入口。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你創作一幅希望讓人感到鄰里歡迎的畫，已有清楚說明；試看者雖能重述說明，卻說未與畫面建立連繫。你想先問他們看見哪些細節及有何感受，而非假定加長說明便可解決。用一至兩句英文描述作品交流落差及下一步。

examples.en: Even with the caption, the painting seems to hang there in silence for these test viewers. I want to ask which details reach them before changing the work.
examples.zh: 即使有說明，畫對這批試看者彷彿仍只默默掛着。改作品前，我想問哪些細節能觸動他們。

examples.en: I do not want my painting to hang there in silence after visitors have understood the caption, so I will ask about their response rather than simply add more explanation.
examples.zh: 我不想訪客讀懂說明後，畫仍只是默默掛着，所以會問他們的反應，而非只加更多解釋。

writing.selfCheckZh: 交代訪客已懂說明卻未連結畫面，用提問反應測作品溝通，不把說明長短或展廳聲量當唯一原因。

takeaways.en: The unfamiliar portrait seemed to hang there in silence until the guide explained the sitter’s connection to the town.
takeaways.zh: 導賞員解釋畫中人與小鎮的關係前，陌生肖像彷彿只默默掛着。

takeaways.en: Without a way to understand the symbols, the picture could hang there in silence for new viewers.
takeaways.zh: 若沒有理解符號的途徑，畫對新觀者可能只默默掛着。

brief.meaningEn: The background, experiences or context that help explain an artwork.
brief.meaningZh: 幫助解釋藝術作品的背景、經歷或脈絡。
brief.grammar: learn/reveal/explore the story behind the artwork; behind points to explanatory background, not a physical position.
brief.register: Natural explanatory noun phrase, not a separate fixed idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 背景可幫理解，卻不一定只有一個正確解讀；需分清史料、藝術家說法與觀者推想。
brief.misconceptionZh: 動人故事不自行證實為真，不能把猜測寫成已查證背景。
brief.outcomeZh: 能詢問或介紹作品背景，清楚標明資料來源與推想。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: An audio guide can reveal the story behind the artwork.

listening.en: The curator explained the story behind the artwork using the artist’s letters, while marking her own interpretation as a possibility rather than a documented fact.
listening.zh: 策展人用藝術家的書信解釋作品背後故事，同時把自己的解讀標為可能，而非有記錄的事實。
listening.promptZh: 策展人怎樣處理背景與解讀？

options.en: She used letters as evidence and separated her interpretation from established facts.
options.zh: 她以書信作證據，把自己的解讀與已確立事實分開。

options.en: She treated an appealing interpretation as if the letters had confirmed it.
options.zh: 她把吸引人的解讀當書信已證實的事。

options.en: She discussed only the physical position of objects behind the frame.
options.zh: 她只談畫框後物件的實際位置。

options.en: She withheld the letters and presented no background at all.
options.zh: 她不提供書信，也完全沒說背景。

listening.explanationZh: using letters 與 marking interpretation 交代兩種資料地位，不是畫框位置。

reply.promptZh: 你怎樣介紹這件作品的背景，又不把推想當事實？
reply.promptEn: How do you introduce the background without presenting your interpretation as fact?

options.en: I use the artist’s letters and identify where I am offering an interpretation.
options.zh: 我用藝術家書信，並指出哪裏是自己的解讀。

options.en: I explain the story behind the artwork and separate documented details from my own reading.
options.zh: 我解釋作品背後故事，並分開有記錄細節與自己的理解。

options.en: I say what the sources show and what remains a possible explanation.
options.zh: 我說明來源顯示甚麼，以及甚麼仍是可能解釋。

options.en: I give the background while making the limits of the evidence clear.
options.zh: 我提供背景，也清楚說明證據限制。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都同時提供背景及來源界線，金句不代表只有一個讀法。

scene.promptZh: 展板交代作品創作時的搬遷經歷，引用畫家日記，但把色彩含意說成待討論。哪句合適？

options.en: The story behind the artwork is limited to where its frame is stored.
options.zh: 作品背後故事只限畫框存放位置。

options.en: The display explains the story behind the artwork while leaving room for interpretation.
options.zh: 展示解釋作品背後故事，同時保留解讀空間。

options.en: The diary confirms every viewer must interpret the colours identically.
options.zh: 日記確認每位觀者都必須同樣解讀顏色。

scene.explanationZh: 日記支持創作背景，顏色含意仍待討論，不能推成唯一讀法。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以當作已查證的作品背景？

options.en: A dated letter describes the artist’s circumstances during the project.
options.zh: 有日期書信描述藝術家創作時處境。

options.en: A recorded interview explains how a commission began.
options.zh: 訪問錄音解釋委約如何開始。

options.en: A visitor invents an appealing story but cannot identify any source for it.
options.zh: 訪客編出動人故事，卻無法指出來源。

contrast.explanationZh: 吸引人不同於已查證；可標為想像，不能當史料。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把一個猜出的愛情故事直接寫成作品背景，因為很感人。哪句較準確？

options.en: Present it as documented background because visitors may remember it easily.
options.zh: 因訪客容易記得，就把它當有記錄背景。

options.en: Leave out the source distinction so the narrative sounds more confident.
options.zh: 刪去來源區分，讓敘述更肯定。

options.en: Check the sources first, and label the story as an interpretation if the evidence does not establish it.
options.zh: 先查來源；若證據未確立，就把故事標為解讀。

dialogue.explanationZh: 敘事吸引力不代替來源，標示解讀仍可讓人討論。

speaking.en: The story behind the artwork helps me understand its setting, but it does not settle every interpretation.
speaking.zh: 作品背後故事幫我理解背景，卻未決定每個解讀。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把背景資料及解讀空間分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為社區雕塑寫介紹，已知它由居民共同委約，但兩份敘述對創作年份不同；你想對照委約文件及作者訪談，再決定可公開的背景，尚不替任何一方猜動機。用一至兩句英文說明。

examples.en: The story behind the artwork includes a community commission, but the two accounts give different dates. I will compare the records before publishing the introduction.
examples.zh: 作品背後故事包括社區委約，但兩份敘述日期不同。我會先比紀錄，再刊介紹。

examples.en: Before explaining the story behind the artwork, we need to check the commission papers against the artist’s interview rather than choose the more appealing account.
examples.zh: 解釋作品背後故事前，我們需把委約文件與藝術家訪問對照，不只選較動人敘述。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用兩份敘述日期不一提出查核，對照文件及訪談，不憑故事動人選史實，也不猜有人故意誤導。

takeaways.en: The story behind the artwork began with a journey the painter described in her diary.
takeaways.zh: 作品背後故事從畫家在日記描述的一段旅程開始。

takeaways.en: I want to learn the story behind the artwork before writing the exhibition note.
takeaways.zh: 寫展覽說明前，我想了解作品背後故事。

brief.meaningEn: Leave a situation or topic behind and continue to a next stage or activity.
brief.meaningZh: 離開一個情況或話題，繼續到下一階段或活動。
brief.grammar: move on from + experience/topic; move on to + next activity; moved on in past.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb for progression; not the physical relocation sense in this lesson.
brief.boundaryZh: 繼續不等於假裝問題沒發生、忘記教訓或沒有感受；也不是未處理必要事項就跳過。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需交代甚麼已告一段落、下一步是甚麼，不把所有換話題都當妥善結束。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述回顧後繼續，保留必要的處理與學習。

sources.sentence: After the review, the group was ready to move on.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: After the review, the group was ready to move on.

listening.en: After discussing why the rehearsal had failed and agreeing a new plan, the group was ready to move on to the next session without repeating the blame.
listening.zh: 討論排練為何失敗並議定新計劃後，小組準備繼續下一節，不再反覆責怪。
listening.promptZh: 小組的 move on 包括甚麼？

options.en: Continue after learning from the problem and agreeing a way forward.
options.zh: 從問題學習、議定前路後繼續。

options.en: Skip reviewing the failure and repeat the old arrangement unchanged.
options.zh: 略過檢討失敗，原封不動重複舊安排。

options.en: Keep the discussion focused only on who should be blamed.
options.zh: 繼續只集中討論該責怪誰。

options.en: Cancel the next session before considering any new plan.
options.zh: 未考慮新計劃便取消下一節。

listening.explanationZh: after discussion and agreement 是前提，繼續不是拒絕回顧或繼續責怪。

reply.promptZh: 你們檢討失敗並定好新計劃後，準備怎樣做？
reply.promptEn: What are you ready to do after reviewing the failure and agreeing a new plan?

options.en: We are ready to begin the next session using what we learnt.
options.zh: 我們準備把所學用於下一節。

options.en: We want to move on rather than keep repeating the blame.
options.zh: 我們想繼續向前，不再反覆責怪。

options.en: We will put the revised plan into practice at the next rehearsal.
options.zh: 我們會在下一次排練實行修訂計劃。

options.en: The review is complete, so we can focus on the next attempt.
options.zh: 檢討已完成，所以可集中下一次嘗試。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都在已回顧的前提下繼續，金句不是否認問題。

scene.promptZh: 會議已把投訴交負責人跟進並記下期限，現在轉到下一個議程。哪句準確？

options.en: We can move on to the next item while keeping the follow-up commitment.
options.zh: 我們可轉下一項，同時保留跟進承諾。

options.en: The follow-up has already been completed because we have discussed the complaint.
options.zh: 我們已討論投訴，所以跟進已完成。

options.en: The follow-up is now optional rather than an agreed commitment.
options.zh: 跟進現在變可選，而非議定承諾。

scene.explanationZh: 議程可推進，但已指定的跟進及期限仍是承諾；討論不等於完成，也不自動變可選。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不像這裏妥善 move on 的例子？

options.en: Using the lesson from a setback in the next attempt.
options.zh: 把挫折所學用於下一次。

options.en: Changing the subject to avoid an unresolved responsibility that still needs a decision.
options.zh: 為逃避仍需決定的責任而轉話題。

options.en: Leaving repeated blame behind after agreeing specific changes.
options.zh: 議定具體改動後，停止反覆責怪。

contrast.explanationZh: 本題問妥善推進，未解責任不是只轉話題便處理了。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說「move on 就不要再記錯誤」，但你們需保存改動避免再犯。哪句較準確？

options.en: Remove the review notes before applying the new plan.
options.zh: 套用新計劃前先刪檢討筆記。

options.en: Continue, but keep the useful lesson and the changes we agreed.
options.zh: 繼續，但保留有用教訓及議定改動。

options.en: Treat any reference to the lesson as proof that the group cannot progress.
options.zh: 把任何提到教訓的話都當小組無法推進的證據。

dialogue.explanationZh: 保留教訓與不再糾纏責怪不同，可帶着所學繼續。

speaking.en: We can move on while keeping the lesson and the changes we agreed.
speaking.zh: 我們可繼續向前，同時保留教訓及議定改動。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再描述推進與保留教訓並存。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫完一段短篇故事，已完成原定修訂；仍有少許不滿，但這次練習目的已達到，想開始新題材，把敘事教訓留下。用一至兩句英文說明下一步。
writing.selfCheckZh: 說明原定修訂及練習目標已完成，下一篇仍用所學，不把推進說成每個作品都必須完美或一概逃避。

examples.en: I am ready to move on to a new story after finishing the planned revision. I will carry the lesson about pacing into my next draft.
examples.zh: 完成原定修訂後，我準備開始新故事。我會把敘事節奏的教訓帶到下一稿。

examples.en: I can move on from this exercise without calling it perfect, using what I learnt when I try a different subject.
examples.zh: 我可不把練習稱作完美，仍告一段落，在試新題材時運用所學。

takeaways.en: After agreeing the follow-up, we moved on to the next part of the meeting.
takeaways.zh: 議定跟進後，我們轉到會議下一部分。

takeaways.en: She moved on from the first attempt while keeping the lesson for her next design.
takeaways.zh: 她在首次嘗試後繼續向前，並為下個設計保留教訓。

titleZh: 彷彿憑空消失得無影無蹤

brief.meaningEn: Disappear completely and seemingly mysteriously, with no apparent trace.
brief.meaningZh: 完全消失，彷彿無法解釋或找不到蹤影。
brief.grammar: disappear/vanish into thin air; disappeared/vanished in past. Negative not disappear into thin air can reject an expectation of instant or complete loss.
brief.register: Established idiom; Cambridge lists disappear and vanish as variants of one idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是物質真的變成空氣，也不直接證明有人偷走或故意隱藏；需再查去向。
brief.misconceptionZh: 覺得找不到不等於已證實永久失去，感覺神秘與實際原因不同。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述突然找不到或反駁憑空消失的說法，保留證據界線。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Traditional bookshops will not disappear into thin air overnight.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The promised funding seemed to have vanished into thin air.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The promised funding seemed to have vanished into thin air.

listening.en: The signed plan seemed to disappear into thin air between the two meetings; nobody could find it, but we had not yet checked the archive log.
listening.zh: 兩次會議之間，已簽計劃彷彿憑空消失；沒人找到，但我們尚未查存檔紀錄。
listening.promptZh: 這句支持哪個結論？

options.en: The plan could not be found then, but its actual whereabouts had not been established.
options.zh: 當時找不到計劃，但尚未確定實際去向。

options.en: The archive log had already proved someone deliberately destroyed it.
options.zh: 存檔紀錄已證明有人故意銷毀。

options.en: The plan remained visible on the meeting table throughout.
options.zh: 計劃一直在會議桌上可見。

options.en: Both meetings were cancelled because no plan had ever existed.
options.zh: 兩次會議因從未有計劃而取消。

listening.explanationZh: seemed 及未查紀錄保留去向未知，不證明銷毀或從未存在。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你想先查存檔紀錄？
reply.promptEn: Why do you want to check the archive log first?

options.en: We cannot find the signed plan and do not yet know where it went.
options.zh: 我們找不到已簽計劃，也未知去了哪裏。

options.en: It seems to have disappeared into thin air, and the log may help trace it.
options.zh: 它彷彿憑空消失，紀錄可能幫忙追查。

options.en: The missing document may have been filed somewhere we have not checked.
options.zh: 失蹤文件可能存放在尚未查的位置。

options.en: We need evidence about the document’s location before deciding what happened.
options.zh: 判斷發生甚麼前，我們需文件位置的證據。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回應找不到但去向未明，金句不是實際物理消失。

scene.promptZh: 昨天仍有的一箱道具，今天在原位找不到，搬運紀錄未查。你想形容目前彷彿完全消失，不指控任何人。哪句合適？

options.en: The box seems to have disappeared into thin air, so we should check the movement records.
options.zh: 箱子彷彿憑空消失，所以應查搬運紀錄。

options.en: Not finding the box establishes that someone stole it.
options.zh: 找不到箱子便確立有人偷走。

options.en: The empty shelf confirms the box was never delivered.
options.zh: 空架確認箱子從未送到。

scene.explanationZh: seems 保留觀察及未知，查紀錄比直接定偷竊或從未送到準確。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論最不宜單靠 disappeared into thin air 得出？

options.en: The speaker cannot see an apparent trace at that point.
options.zh: 說話者當時找不到明顯蹤影。

options.en: A specific person deliberately removed the object.
options.zh: 某個特定人士故意拿走物件。

options.en: The disappearance may feel mysterious to the speaker.
options.zh: 消失對說話者可能顯得神秘。

contrast.explanationZh: 比喻不能提供拿走者身份或動機。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴找不到文件，就想把 disappeared into thin air 寫成已證實被偷。哪句較準確？

options.en: Use the phrase as evidence of theft without looking at where files were moved.
options.zh: 不查檔案移到哪裏，就把片語當偷竊證據。

options.en: Keep the missing-file description separate from any claim about who caused it.
options.zh: 把文件失蹤描述與誰造成的宣稱分開。

options.en: Name the last reader as responsible before checking whether the file was archived.
options.zh: 未查是否存檔，就指最後閱讀者負責。

dialogue.explanationZh: 找不到是觀察，誰造成及動機仍需證據。

speaking.en: The notes seem to have disappeared into thin air, but we should check the shared folder before drawing conclusions.
speaking.zh: 筆記彷彿憑空消失，但下結論前應查共享資料夾。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再描述失蹤感及待查的事。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：同學擔心社團轉到線上聯絡後，過往建立的友情會立即消失。你想指出友誼不會自動憑空消失，但仍需主動相處，不保證一定長存。用一至兩句英文回應。
writing.selfCheckZh: 反駁媒介改變便立即消失的推論，也保留持續聯絡需要；不把不會憑空消失變成永遠不用投入。

examples.en: Our friendship will not disappear into thin air just because the club now meets online. We still need to make time to talk.
examples.zh: 友誼不會只因社團現在網上聚會就憑空消失。我們仍需留時間聊天。

examples.en: The connections we built will not simply vanish into thin air, but keeping them strong will take continued contact.
examples.zh: 我們建立的連繫不會就此憑空消失，但維持深厚仍需繼續聯絡。

takeaways.en: The promised support seemed to vanish into thin air when nobody could find the agreement.
takeaways.zh: 沒人找到協議時，承諾的支援彷彿憑空消失。

takeaways.en: A long friendship does not disappear into thin air simply because two friends move to different cities.
takeaways.zh: 長久友誼不會只因兩人搬到不同城市就憑空消失。

titleEn: standing in front of an original artwork
titleZh: 親身站在藝術原作面前

target.pattern: \bstand(?:s|ing)? in front of an original artwork\b|\bstood in front of an original artwork\b

brief.meaningEn: View the physical original artwork directly, in contrast with viewing a reproduction or digital image.
brief.meaningZh: 親身直接觀看實體藝術原作，與看複製品或數碼影像區分。
brief.grammar: standing in front of an original artwork; stand/stood; original here identifies the work itself, not an opinion about its quality.
brief.register: Natural descriptive construction, not an idiom. Direct viewing offers different access but is not automatically a better interpretation.
brief.boundaryZh: 親眼看可見尺寸、表面等特點，卻不自動證明畫作來源、所有背景或每種解讀。
brief.misconceptionZh: 數碼影像也有用途；應說明觀看方式帶來甚麼資料，而非一概貶低複製品。
brief.outcomeZh: 能比較實體與影像觀看的具體差異及限制。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.expression: standing in front of an original artwork
sources.sentence: Standing in front of an original artwork can change your impression.

listening.en: Standing in front of an original artwork, I noticed the thickness of the paint and its scale in the room, details that were harder to judge from the small online image.
listening.zh: 站在藝術原作前，我留意到顏料厚度及作品在房間的大小，這些細節在小網上影像較難判斷。
listening.promptZh: 親身觀看提供了甚麼？

options.en: A clearer sense of surface and physical scale in this case.
options.zh: 在這例子中較清楚感受到表面及實體大小。

options.en: Proof of every detail in the artist’s life.
options.zh: 藝術家生平每項細節的證據。

options.en: Only the same flat thumbnail, with no view of the physical object.
options.zh: 只看相同平面縮圖，未見實體物件。

options.en: Confirmation that no digital image could be useful for any purpose.
options.zh: 確認任何數碼影像對任何用途都無用。

listening.explanationZh: 顏料厚度與房間中尺寸是給定差異，沒有生平或數碼影像全無用的證據。

reply.promptZh: 這次親身觀看與看小網上影像有甚麼不同？
reply.promptEn: How was this visit different from looking at the small online image?

options.en: I could judge its scale against the room and see the paint surface.
options.zh: 我可對照房間判斷尺寸，看到顏料表面。

options.en: Standing in front of an original artwork let me notice its texture and physical size.
options.zh: 站在藝術原作前，讓我留意質感及實體大小。

options.en: The surface details were easier to notice in person.
options.zh: 親身看較易留意表面細節。

options.en: I gained a better sense of how the work occupied the space.
options.zh: 我較能感受作品在空間中的大小。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述實際可觀察差異，不把直接觀看當全知。

scene.promptZh: 你看原作時，才留意畫布邊緣的厚塗；之前縮圖沒顯出。哪句有根據？

options.en: The visit tells me everything about the artist’s intentions.
options.zh: 到訪告訴我藝術家全部意圖。

options.en: Standing in front of an original artwork helped me see a surface detail missing from the thumbnail.
options.zh: 站在原作前，幫我看見縮圖沒有的表面細節。

options.en: The thumbnail had already shown the same thick edge clearly.
options.zh: 縮圖早已清楚顯示相同厚邊。

scene.explanationZh: 題目只支持厚塗這項觀看差異，不是全部意圖。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能由親身看到原作單獨確定？

options.en: How large it appears relative to the viewer and room.
options.zh: 它相對觀者及房間顯得多大。

options.en: Visible features of its surface under the display lighting.
options.zh: 展示照明下可見的表面特徵。

options.en: The complete ownership history without checking any records.
options.zh: 不查任何紀錄就知道完整收藏歷史。

contrast.explanationZh: 直接看可提供視覺資料，完整收藏歷史仍需來源。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說只要站在原作前，就不需查創作日期及來源。哪句回應較準確？

options.en: Direct viewing helps us notice the object, but dates and provenance still need reliable records.
options.zh: 直接看幫我們留意物件，但日期及來源仍需可靠紀錄。

options.en: Replace the catalogue date with whatever period the paint surface suggests to us.
options.zh: 用顏料表面讓我們聯想到的年代取代目錄日期。

options.en: Treat the feeling of being close to the object as evidence of its whole history.
options.zh: 把靠近物件的感受當它完整歷史的證據。

dialogue.explanationZh: 觀察物件與查歷史是不同資料工作。

speaking.en: Standing in front of an original artwork helped me notice its surface, not discover every fact about its history.
speaking.zh: 站在藝術原作前，幫我留意表面，而非發現其歷史每項事實。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把直接觀察與歷史查證分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替無法到場的同學寫展覽筆記，發現一件原作在側面照明下有不同陰影，照片只呈現正面。用一至兩句英文報告親眼觀察，並說明照片仍可幫他先看構圖。
writing.selfCheckZh: 報告實際移動時看到的陰影，也保留照片看構圖的用途，不把不同觀看方式寫成只有一種有用。

examples.en: Standing in front of an original artwork, I could watch its shadows change as I moved sideways. The photograph still helps my classmate study the composition.
examples.zh: 站在藝術原作前，我可隨側移看到陰影改變。照片仍幫同學研究構圖。

examples.en: I noticed the side-lit shadows while standing in front of an original artwork, so I will describe them in the notes alongside the front-view photograph.
examples.zh: 站在藝術原作前，我留意側光陰影，所以會在筆記中配正面照片描述它們。

takeaways.en: Standing in front of an original artwork gave me a clearer sense of its scale beside the doorway.
takeaways.zh: 站在原作前，讓我對照門口更清楚感受它的尺寸。

takeaways.en: She described the visible texture after standing in front of an original artwork.
takeaways.zh: 站在藝術原作前觀看後，她描述可見質感。

brief.meaningEn: Provide or use enough money to meet ordinary living or operating expenses.
brief.meaningZh: 提供或使用足夠金錢支付日常生活或營運開支。
brief.grammar: the work pays the bills; earn enough to pay the bills; paid in past. Literal bills support a broader livelihood expression.
brief.register: Conventional everyday wording; not a special promise of wealth or profit.
brief.boundaryZh: 能付開支不表示富裕、喜歡工作或已儲夠擴張資金；稱讚也未必帶來收入。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要分清欣賞、曝光及實際收入，不能用讚好數代替支出與報酬資料。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述生活或營運費需要，與其他價值分開。

listening.en: In the story, her illustration commissions pay the bills, while the experimental paintings are work she values but has not sold.
listening.zh: 故事中，她的插畫委約支付日常開支；實驗畫作是她珍惜、但未出售的工作。
listening.promptZh: 哪項收入與開支關係有根據？

options.en: The commissions provide ordinary income; the valued paintings have not yet sold.
options.zh: 委約提供日常收入；珍惜的畫作尚未賣出。

options.en: The unsold paintings already cover her regular expenses.
options.zh: 未出售畫作已支付她平常開支。

options.en: She dislikes the commissions because they provide income.
options.zh: 她因委約帶來收入而不喜歡它們。

options.en: All the commission income is reserved for expanding a studio after bills are paid elsewhere.
options.zh: 委約收入全留作擴大工作室，帳單由其他來源支付。

listening.explanationZh: 收入來源與珍惜的創作分開描述，未交代對委約喜惡或擴張安排。

reply.promptZh: 故事中，插畫委約怎樣支援她繼續創作？
reply.promptEn: How do the illustration commissions support her work in the story?

options.en: The income covers her regular expenses.
options.zh: 收入支付她平常開支。

options.en: The commissions pay the bills while she develops the paintings.
options.zh: 她發展畫作時，委約支付日常開支。

options.en: Paid illustration work provides money for everyday costs.
options.zh: 有酬插畫工作提供日常費用。

options.en: She can meet ordinary expenses through the commissions.
options.zh: 她可透過委約應付平常開支。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明日常收入功能，不推斷富裕或不喜歡工作。

scene.promptZh: 虛構樂手故事中，教學收入支付房租及基本費用，原創演出暫未有收入。哪句準確？

options.en: The unpaid performances already cover the rent.
options.zh: 無酬演出已支付房租。

options.en: Teaching pays the bills while the original performances develop.
options.zh: 原創演出發展期間，教學支付日常開支。

options.en: Receiving teaching income proves the musician dislikes composing.
options.zh: 獲教學收入證明樂手不喜歡作曲。

scene.explanationZh: 題目只交代收入分工，不提供喜惡結論。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以證明工作 pays the bills？

options.en: The income meets the stated regular expenses.
options.zh: 收入應付所說平常開支。

options.en: A record shows ordinary costs covered by the paid work.
options.zh: 紀錄顯示日常費用由有酬工作支付。

options.en: Many people praise the work, but no income or covered costs are reported.
options.zh: 很多人讚賞作品，卻未有收入或已付費用資料。

contrast.explanationZh: 稱讚不等於收入，需看付開支的資料。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴見畫作很多讚好，就想寫畫家已能靠它付生活費，卻沒售價或收入資料。哪句建議最好？

options.en: Distinguish appreciation from income before claiming it pays the bills.
options.zh: 宣稱作品支付生活費前，先分清欣賞與收入。

options.en: Use the number of likes as if each represented a paid sale.
options.zh: 把每個讚好當一次付費銷售。

options.en: Treat an offer of exposure as confirmation that ordinary costs are covered.
options.zh: 把曝光機會當日常費用已付的確認。

dialogue.explanationZh: 要有實際收入與費用資料，不能用人氣替代。

speaking.en: The commissions pay the bills, but that alone does not tell us how she feels about the work.
speaking.zh: 委約支付日常開支，但這本身未告訴我們她對工作的感受。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清收入功能與個人感受。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：虛構小劇場本月的紀念冊收入足夠支付租金及電費，免費導賞有教育作用但沒帶來收入。你整理資源報告，想分清支付開支與教育價值，不說哪項較值得。用一至兩句英文說明。

examples.en: In this month’s report, booklet sales pay the bills, while the free tours serve an educational purpose. Those are different contributions to the theatre.
examples.zh: 在本月報告中，紀念冊銷售支付開支，免費導賞則有教育作用。兩者對劇場的貢獻不同。

examples.en: The theatre uses booklet income to pay the bills without treating ticket-free learning as worthless.
examples.zh: 劇場用紀念冊收入支付開支，並不因此把免費學習當沒有價值。

writing.selfCheckZh: 按已給收入與開支資料描述紀念冊作用，也保留導賞教育價值，不用收入比較代替整體價值評斷。

takeaways.en: In the novel, his repair work pays the bills while he studies design.
takeaways.zh: 小說中，他讀設計期間靠維修工作支付日常開支。

takeaways.en: The exhibition attracted praise, but ticket income did not yet pay the bills.
takeaways.zh: 展覽獲讚賞，但門票收入尚未足付開支。

titleEn: put your money where your mouth is
titleZh: 以實際行動支持口頭主張

target.pattern: \bput(?:s|ting)? (?:(?:my money where my|your money where your|his money where his|her money where her) mouth is|(?:our money where our|their money where their|your money where your) mouths are)\b

brief.meaningEn: Support what you say you believe with practical commitment, often including spending money.
brief.meaningZh: 用實際投入支持自己所說的信念，常包括花錢支持。
brief.grammar: put my/your/his/her money where my/your/his/her mouth is; put our/their money where our/their mouths are; match the same owner on both sides. Put is unchanged in past.
brief.register: Informal idiom; can sound challenging or direct, so consider the relationship and ability to contribute.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點是行動與主張一致，不是逼人花超出能力的錢，也不是證明花最多者最真誠。
brief.misconceptionZh: 支持方式須看情境，不能把每種善意都量成付款額；要指出所主張及相應行動。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把公開支持連到具體可行投入，避免不合理施壓。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.expression: put your money where your mouth is
sources.sentence: If you value local music, put your money where your mouth is and buy a ticket.

listening.en: We say local theatre matters, so we decided to put our money where our mouths are by buying tickets within our budget rather than only sharing praise.
listening.zh: 我們說本地劇場重要，所以決定在預算內買票，以實際行動支持所說，而不只分享稱讚。
listening.promptZh: 這個決定怎樣回應口頭支持？

options.en: They matched their stated support with a concrete purchase they could afford.
options.zh: 他們以可負擔的具體購買配合口頭支持。

options.en: They replaced attendance with praise while avoiding any practical involvement.
options.zh: 他們以稱讚取代到場，避免實際參與。

options.en: They judged everyone’s sincerity only by the amount spent.
options.zh: 他們只按花費評斷每人真誠。

options.en: They bought tickets for an unrelated event without expressing support for theatre.
options.zh: 他們未支持劇場，買了無關活動門票。

listening.explanationZh: 劇場主張與買票一致，within budget 保留能力限制，沒有按花費評人。

reply.promptZh: 你們怎樣把「本地劇場重要」變成可行支持？
reply.promptEn: How did you turn your support for local theatre into something practical?

options.en: We bought tickets we could afford instead of stopping at praise.
options.zh: 我們買能負擔的門票，而不止於稱讚。

options.en: We put our money where our mouths are and bought tickets within our budget.
options.zh: 我們以行動支持所說，在預算內買票。

options.en: We turned our stated support into a concrete booking.
options.zh: 我們把口頭支持變成具體預訂。

options.en: We chose an affordable performance and paid to attend.
options.zh: 我們選可負擔演出，付費到場。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代主張及可行行動，金句不要求超出能力。

scene.promptZh: 你常說校刊值得支持，這期決定用已預留的小額預算訂閱，不只稱讚。哪句合適？

options.en: I put my money where my mouth is by subscribing within my budget.
options.zh: 我在預算內訂閱，以行動支持所說。

options.en: My praise proves the magazine has already received subscription income from me.
options.zh: 我的稱讚證明刊物已收到我的訂閱費。

options.en: Only the person who pays the highest amount can genuinely value the magazine.
options.zh: 只有付最多的人才可真正珍惜刊物。

scene.explanationZh: 具體訂閱與主張相配，讚賞不等於已付款，金額也不定真誠。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不像這裏 put your money where your mouth is？

options.en: Backing a stated cause with an appropriate concrete commitment.
options.zh: 以恰當具體投入支持所主張的事。

options.en: Paying for the affordable event you have publicly encouraged others to support.
options.zh: 付款參與曾公開鼓勵別人支持、自己負擔得起的活動。

options.en: Continuing to praise a project while refusing a promised contribution you could readily make.
options.zh: 繼續讚項目，卻拒絕作出已答應、能輕鬆做到的投入。

contrast.explanationZh: 本課焦點是說與做一致，不是評價不能負擔者。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想用這句話逼所有人捐同一筆錢，卻不知道各人能力。哪句較體諒？

options.en: Set the same payment as the only way to show commitment.
options.zh: 把相同付款定為唯一投入方式。

options.en: Invite a practical contribution that fits each person’s circumstances instead of using spending as a test of sincerity.
options.zh: 邀請各人按情況作實際投入，不以花費測真誠。

options.en: Treat an inability to pay the requested sum as proof that the person never cared.
options.zh: 把付不起所求金額當從未關心的證據。

dialogue.explanationZh: 鼓勵實際支持仍需尊重能力，不能把付款量當唯一真誠標準。

speaking.en: I want to put my money where my mouth is by supporting the event in a way I can afford.
speaking.zh: 我想用能負擔的方式支持活動，以行動配合所說。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再連結主張、投入及能力。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在社團會議主張保留維修而非丟棄的習慣，現在有一場維修工具共用計劃，費用在你已定預算內。用一至兩句英文說明自己的具體支持，不要求別人跟你付款。
writing.selfCheckZh: 把自己的維修主張與工具計劃投入連起來，保留預算界線，不指其他人必須同額付款。

examples.en: I can put my money where my mouth is by contributing to the shared repair tools within my budget. That supports the repair habit I have been promoting.
examples.zh: 我可在預算內為共享維修工具出資，以行動支持所說。這支持我一直提倡的維修習慣。

examples.en: I have argued for repairing things, so I will put my money where my mouth is with an affordable contribution to the tool scheme.
examples.zh: 我曾主張維修物品，所以會以能負擔的工具計劃出資，實踐所說。

takeaways.en: We put our money where our mouths are by buying the accessible edition we had asked the publisher to produce.
takeaways.zh: 我們購買曾要求出版社製作的無障礙版本，以行動支持所說。

takeaways.en: She chose to put her money where her mouth is with a contribution she could afford.
takeaways.zh: 她選擇以能負擔的出資實踐所說。

brief.meaningEn: Have a substantial helpful effect, often from something that seems relatively small.
brief.meaningZh: 帶來相當大的幫助，常指看似不多的事所產生的作用。
brief.grammar: go a long way towards + -ing / in + -ing; goes/went/gone; very intensifies the same helpful-effect idiom.
brief.register: Common distance metaphor; this lesson is helpful effect, not literal travel or predicting a successful career.
brief.boundaryZh: 很有幫助不等於單靠它已解決全部，也不一定是最重要因素；需說明作用。
brief.misconceptionZh: 小行動可有用，但不能不看情境就保證任何小事都有效。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述具體小投入帶來的幫助，保留其他需要。

listening.en: A clear welcome message went a long way towards helping new volunteers feel less uncertain, although they still needed practical training.
listening.zh: 清楚歡迎訊息大大幫新義工減少不確定感，但他們仍需實際訓練。
listening.promptZh: 訊息的作用與限制是甚麼？

options.en: It helped newcomers feel more secure without replacing practical training.
options.zh: 它幫新人較安心，卻未取代實際訓練。

options.en: It completed all the training before any practical tasks began.
options.zh: 它在實作前完成全部訓練。

options.en: It had no effect because the volunteers still needed training.
options.zh: 因義工仍需訓練，所以訊息毫無作用。

options.en: It described the physical distance volunteers had travelled.
options.zh: 它描述義工走過的實際距離。

listening.explanationZh: help less uncertain 交代幫助，although 保留訓練，不是全完成或沒用。

reply.promptZh: 短短歡迎訊息對新義工有甚麼作用？
reply.promptEn: What difference did the short welcome message make for new volunteers?

options.en: It made the first contact feel clearer and less uncertain.
options.zh: 它令首次接觸較清楚，少點不確定。

options.en: It went a long way towards helping them feel welcome.
options.zh: 它大大幫他們感到受歡迎。

options.en: It was a small step that gave newcomers useful reassurance.
options.zh: 它是一小步，給新人有用的安心感。

options.en: The clear introduction helped them feel more ready to ask questions.
options.zh: 清楚介紹幫他們較願意提問。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出具體幫助，不把訊息當完整訓練。

scene.promptZh: 你替難懂表格加一個清楚填寫例子，測試時新生少問重複問題，但仍有個別欄位待改。哪句準確？

options.en: One example made further form improvements unnecessary.
options.zh: 一個例子令進一步改表不再需要。

options.en: The example went a long way towards making the form easier to use.
options.zh: 例子大大幫表格變得較易用。

options.en: The remaining problems establish that the example helped nobody.
options.zh: 剩餘問題確立例子沒幫任何人。

scene.explanationZh: 少重複問題支持幫助，剩餘改動不抹去作用，也非全解。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論最不宜由 went a long way 得出？

options.en: A step contributed substantially towards a helpful outcome.
options.zh: 一個步驟對有利結果有相當貢獻。

options.en: Further work may still be needed.
options.zh: 可能仍需進一步工作。

options.en: That single step must have completed every part of the task.
options.zh: 單一這步必定完成任務所有部分。

contrast.explanationZh: 有相當幫助與完全完成不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說一個例子很有幫助，所以想取消測試已發現的其餘表格修訂。哪句回應最好？

options.en: Keep the helpful example and address the remaining problems the test identified.
options.zh: 保留有幫助的例子，並處理測試找出的其餘問題。

options.en: Use the improvement as evidence that the remaining difficult fields now work.
options.zh: 把改善當其餘難填欄位已可用的證據。

options.en: Remove the example because it did not solve every issue by itself.
options.zh: 因例子未獨力解全部，就刪掉它。

dialogue.explanationZh: 既可肯定作用，也可繼續修訂，不是全有全無。

speaking.en: A clear explanation can go a long way, even when further practice is still needed.
speaking.zh: 清楚解釋可大有幫助，即使仍需更多練習。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再描述幫助與尚餘需要。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：兩位同學合作時曾有誤會，其中一人具體承認漏傳資料並道歉，對話氣氛改善，但分工仍需重訂。用一至兩句英文描述道歉的幫助及下一步。
writing.selfCheckZh: 把承認漏傳及道歉連到信任或氣氛改善，同時保留更新與分工需議定，不保證道歉解決全部。

examples.en: The specific apology went a long way towards rebuilding trust, but we still need to agree how to share updates.
examples.zh: 具體道歉大大幫重建信任，但我們仍需議定怎樣分享更新。

examples.en: Admitting the missed message can go a very long way in improving the conversation, while the roles still need to be clarified.
examples.zh: 承認漏傳訊息可大大幫改善對話，但分工仍需釐清。

glossary.en: roles still need to be clarified

takeaways.en: A patient answer went a long way towards making the new member feel included.
takeaways.zh: 耐心回答大大幫新組員感到被接納。

takeaways.en: Checking the instructions together can go a very long way, though the group still has to do the work.
takeaways.zh: 一起核對指引可大有幫助，但小組仍需實際做工作。

titleZh: 人與人之間的口碑推薦

brief.meaningEn: Information or recommendations passed from person to person rather than only through formal advertising.
brief.meaningZh: 由人傳給人的資訊或推薦，而非只透過正式廣告。
brief.grammar: by/through word of mouth; a word-of-mouth recommendation uses hyphens before a noun; target noun phrase here.
brief.register: Established expression; recommendations may be spoken or shared personally online.
brief.boundaryZh: 不必只靠聲音，也不保證內容準確、完全自發或每人都喜歡；與廣告可能同時存在。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需有實際人傳人推薦資料，不只見人氣上升就決定來源。
brief.outcomeZh: 能辨識推薦途徑，與廣告及可信度分開。

listening.en: The café’s first regulars told friends about the welcoming service, and many new visitors said they had heard about it through word of mouth rather than the poster outside.
listening.zh: 咖啡店最初熟客向朋友介紹親切服務，許多新訪客說經人際推薦得知，而非外面海報。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼資料支持口碑來源？

options.en: New visitors reported recommendations from other people.
options.zh: 新訪客表示得到別人推薦。

options.en: Only the café owner assumed a busy room meant the poster had worked.
options.zh: 只是店主假定客人多代表海報有效。

options.en: Visitors said nobody had mentioned the café to them.
options.zh: 訪客說沒人向他們提過咖啡店。

options.en: The account attributes every visit to a paid advertisement.
options.zh: 敘述把每次到訪都歸因付費廣告。

listening.explanationZh: 朋友介紹及訪客回報是人傳人資料，非只看人數。

reply.promptZh: 許多新訪客說怎樣知道這家咖啡店？
reply.promptEn: How did many new visitors say they had found the café?

options.en: Friends recommended the service to them.
options.zh: 朋友向他們推薦服務。

options.en: They heard about it through word of mouth.
options.zh: 他們經口碑推薦得知。

options.en: People who had visited passed the recommendation on.
options.zh: 曾到訪的人把推薦傳開。

options.en: They followed personal suggestions rather than noticing the outside poster.
options.zh: 他們聽個人建議，而非留意外面海報。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述人傳人途徑，金句不證明推薦必定準確。

scene.promptZh: 讀書會成員在私人訊息向朋友分享親身參加經驗，朋友再邀其他人；沒有付費宣傳。哪句有根據？

options.en: Word of mouth helped people discover the group.
options.zh: 口碑推薦幫大家認識小組。

options.en: A paid campaign is the only reported source of the invitations.
options.zh: 付費宣傳是邀請唯一已報告來源。

options.en: Private written messages cannot carry personal recommendations.
options.zh: 私人文字訊息不能帶個人推薦。

scene.explanationZh: 個人經驗逐人傳開，寫成訊息也可口碑傳播，不必只口述。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以確定人們經 word of mouth 得知活動？

options.en: Attendees identify a friend’s recommendation as their source.
options.zh: 出席者指出來源是朋友推薦。

options.en: People describe passing a personal recommendation to their neighbours.
options.zh: 大家描述向鄰居傳個人推薦。

options.en: Attendance rose, but nobody has asked how visitors heard about the event.
options.zh: 出席增加，卻沒人查訪客如何得知活動。

contrast.explanationZh: 人數本身不足以確定傳播來源。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴只見活動滿座，就想把宣傳全歸功口碑，卻沒查任何來源。哪句建議最好？

options.en: Record the full room as proof that no advertisement contributed.
options.zh: 把滿座記為沒有廣告貢獻的證據。

options.en: Ask attendees how they heard about it before assigning credit to word of mouth.
options.zh: 把功勞歸口碑前，先問出席者如何得知。

options.en: Use the organiser’s preferred channel as the reported source for everyone.
options.zh: 把主辦者偏好管道當每人所報來源。

dialogue.explanationZh: 要實際來源資料，口碑及廣告亦可並存。

speaking.en: Word of mouth brought new visitors, but we still need to check what they actually experienced.
speaking.zh: 口碑推薦帶來新訪客，但我們仍需查他們實際體驗。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清推薦途徑與體驗品質。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替學校選一本新社團用書，幾位同學親身讀過後互相推薦，但你仍要查看程度及內容是否適合。用一至兩句英文描述知道此書的途徑及仍需的查核。
writing.selfCheckZh: 交代同學親讀後互推的途徑，保留程度與內容需查，不把口碑當一定適合的保證。

examples.en: We discovered the book through word of mouth from students who had read it. We still need to check whether its level suits the club.
examples.zh: 我們經讀過此書的同學口碑推薦得知，但仍需查程度是否適合社團。

examples.en: Word of mouth made us curious about the book, but we will review the content before choosing it for the group.
examples.zh: 口碑推薦令我們對書好奇，但替小組選書前仍會檢視內容。

takeaways.en: The repair club grew through word of mouth as neighbours shared their experiences.
takeaways.zh: 鄰居分享經驗，維修社團經口碑推薦成長。

takeaways.en: Word of mouth led me to the course, and the sample lesson helped me judge its level.
takeaways.zh: 口碑推薦讓我知道課程，試堂則幫我判斷程度。

brief.meaningEn: Produce a meaningful practical change, often an improvement, in the situation being discussed.
brief.meaningZh: 在所談情況帶來有意義的實際改變，常指改善。
brief.grammar: make a (real/big) difference to + person/situation; make all the difference is an emphatic same-idiom variant; made in past. State the effect rather than assuming sole causation.
brief.register: Conventional difference idiom/collocation with real, big and all the difference expressing emphasis; not necessarily the only decisive cause.
brief.boundaryZh: 不等於解決全部、獨自造成所有結果或人人同樣受益；需指明改善資料。
brief.misconceptionZh: 投入、花費或好意不自動證明成效，要看實際變化。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體改變支持成效說法，避免只報做過甚麼。

listening.en: The clearer bus-stop signs made a real difference to first-time visitors: fewer people went to the wrong entrance, though the evening route still confused some of them.
listening.zh: 較清楚巴士站告示對初訪者帶來實在改善：較少人走錯入口，但晚間路線仍令部分人混淆。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼支持實在改善？

options.en: Fewer first-time visitors used the wrong entrance.
options.zh: 較少初訪者走錯入口。

options.en: Every visitor now understands every evening route.
options.zh: 每位訪客現在都懂所有晚間路線。

options.en: The organisers printed more signs but did not check any result.
options.zh: 主辦者印更多告示，卻沒查任何結果。

options.en: The entrance changed location, so no comparison was possible.
options.zh: 入口改位置，所以無法比較。

listening.explanationZh: 較少走錯是具體結果；晚間仍有困難，不能擴為全解。

reply.promptZh: 新告示對初訪者有甚麼幫助？
reply.promptEn: How did the new signs help first-time visitors?

options.en: Fewer of them went to the wrong entrance.
options.zh: 較少人走錯入口。

options.en: The clearer signs made a real difference to finding the entrance.
options.zh: 較清楚告示對找入口帶來實在改善。

options.en: The directions reduced how often newcomers used the wrong entrance.
options.zh: 指路減少新人走錯入口的次數。

options.en: The route into the venue became easier for newcomers to follow.
options.zh: 新人較容易跟路線進場。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述實際改善，金句不保證每條路線已清楚。

scene.promptZh: 同一批學生試用加大字體的說明後，閱讀錯誤減少，你還未測所有學生。哪句合適？

options.en: The larger text made a real difference for the students in the trial.
options.zh: 加大字體為試用學生帶來實在改善。

options.en: A trial with these students proves the change works equally for every reader.
options.zh: 這批學生試用證明改動對所有讀者同樣有效。

options.en: The change has no value because not every reader has been tested.
options.zh: 因未測每位讀者，改動就沒價值。

scene.explanationZh: 可報所測結果，不推成普遍一致，也不抹去已有改善。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以證明某改動 made a real difference？

options.en: Repeated observations show fewer mistakes after the change.
options.zh: 重複觀察顯示改動後較少錯誤。

options.en: The team spent a long time on it but has no information about what changed.
options.zh: 團隊花很久，卻無改變了甚麼的資料。

options.en: The affected users describe a specific task becoming easier.
options.zh: 受影響使用者描述某項工作變容易。

contrast.explanationZh: 努力本身不是效果，需要觀察實際改變。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把「花了很多時間改版」寫成已證明有成效，卻還沒讓學生試用。哪句建議最好？

options.en: Ask students to try the task and look for specific changes before claiming impact.
options.zh: 宣稱成效前，讓學生試做並看具體變化。

options.en: Use the hours spent as the result instead of checking what readers can do.
options.zh: 不查讀者能做甚麼，把工時當結果。

options.en: Describe the improved appearance as proof that every task is easier.
options.zh: 把外觀改善當每項工作都變容易的證據。

dialogue.explanationZh: 成效要對照使用任務，不能只看投入及外觀。

speaking.en: The change made a real difference in the trial, but we still need to check who else it helps.
speaking.zh: 改動在試用中帶來實在改善，但仍需查還幫到誰。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把試用結果與推廣範圍分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們把社團會議結尾改成逐人確認負責事項，下一周漏交接減少，但偶有更改仍未通知。用一至兩句英文描述具體改善及仍需處理的部分。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用漏交接減少支持改善，保留會後變更需通知，不把完成一次核對當所有溝通已解。

examples.en: Confirming each person’s task made a real difference to handovers: fewer items were missed, though late changes still need a clearer update process.
examples.zh: 確認每人工作對交接帶來實在改善：漏項減少，但臨時更改仍需較清楚更新流程。

examples.en: The final task check can make a real difference, but we should also agree how to communicate changes after the meeting.
examples.zh: 最後工作核對可帶來實在改善，但我們也應議定會後怎樣傳達更改。

takeaways.en: The extra reading light made a real difference for the students at the back table.
takeaways.zh: 額外閱讀燈為後桌學生帶來實在改善。

takeaways.en: A clear handover can make a real difference when the next group takes over.
takeaways.zh: 下一組接手時，清楚交接可帶來實在改善。

brief.meaningEn: A person or source of support that helps someone develop confidence, capability or success.
brief.meaningZh: 幫助別人發展信心、能力或取得成果的人或支援力量。
brief.grammar: be the wind beneath someone’s wings; match possessive to the supported person. Name what the support actually involved.
brief.register: Expressive flight metaphor, often appreciative or emotional; not a literal explanation of flight.
brief.boundaryZh: 支持重要不表示代做全部、唯一原因或受助者沒有投入；需要保留其努力。
brief.misconceptionZh: 空泛稱讚不如說清支持，亦不能因有人指導就抹去受助者的責任與貢獻。
brief.outcomeZh: 能感謝具體支持，同時承認本人投入。

sources.sentence: Their first teacher was the wind beneath their wings when the young actors began.

listening.en: Our mentor was the wind beneath our wings: her patient feedback helped us improve the first performance, while the cast still had to rehearse the changes.
listening.zh: 導師是助我們展翅的力量：她耐心回饋幫我們改善首次演出，而演員仍需排練改動。
listening.promptZh: 這個飛行比喻怎樣分配作用？

options.en: The mentor supported improvement, and the cast still practised.
options.zh: 導師支援改善，演員仍有練習。

options.en: The mentor performed every role in place of the cast.
options.zh: 導師代演員演每個角色。

options.en: The cast improved without receiving any useful response.
options.zh: 演員沒有任何有用回應就改善。

options.en: The feedback was a reward given only after the final performance had ended.
options.zh: 回饋只是最後演出結束後才給的獎勵。

listening.explanationZh: feedback helped 與 still rehearse 共同說明支援及本人投入，不是代做。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你們想特別感謝導師？
reply.promptEn: Why do you want to thank the mentor in particular?

options.en: Her patient feedback helped us improve while we practised.
options.zh: 我們練習時，她耐心回饋幫我們改善。

options.en: She was the wind beneath our wings, giving us patient guidance through the first performance.
options.zh: 她是助我們展翅的力量，耐心指導我們走過首次演出。

options.en: She helped us see what to change and encouraged us to keep trying.
options.zh: 她幫我們看見要改甚麼，鼓勵繼續嘗試。

options.en: Her support helped us turn the rehearsal notes into a better performance.
options.zh: 她的支援幫我們把排練筆記化成較好演出。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都有具體支持理由，金句不抹去演員排練。

scene.promptZh: 同學在你首次辦展時耐心聽構思、幫你找改進方向，你仍親自製作。你想用感謝的比喻。哪句合適？

options.en: She was the wind beneath my wings as I developed the exhibition.
options.zh: 我發展展覽時，她是助我展翅的力量。

options.en: Her support means I made no contribution to the exhibition.
options.zh: 她支援表示我對展覽毫無貢獻。

options.en: Calling her supportive establishes that she made every object herself.
options.zh: 稱她有支援就確立每件物件都她做。

scene.explanationZh: 給方向與聆聽是助力，與代做所有不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論最不宜單憑這個支持比喻得出？

options.en: Someone’s help was important to the speaker.
options.zh: 某人的幫忙對說話者重要。

options.en: The supported person necessarily did none of the work.
options.zh: 受助者必定完全沒做工作。

options.en: Context should explain the guidance or encouragement involved.
options.zh: 情境應說清有何指導或鼓勵。

contrast.explanationZh: 感謝助力不否定本人努力。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把感謝導師的句子改成「學生成功全由導師代做」，你知道學生有反覆練習。哪句較準確？

options.en: Credit the guidance and the students’ practice rather than replacing one with the other.
options.zh: 同時肯定指導及學生練習，不用其中一方取代另一方。

options.en: Leave out the rehearsals so the thank-you sounds stronger.
options.zh: 為讓感謝更強，刪去排練投入。

options.en: Describe the students’ practice as unrelated because a mentor helped.
options.zh: 因導師幫過，就說學生練習無關。

dialogue.explanationZh: 感謝可以具體而不誇大成唯一或代做全部。

speaking.en: She was the wind beneath our wings, and we still had to put her advice into practice.
speaking.zh: 她是助我們展翅的力量，而我們仍需實踐她的建議。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再感謝支持並承認自己投入。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你想參加首次攝影實作，原本沒有合用相機，也不熟悉設施預約。同學借器材並幫你找到預約途徑，你得以參與；拍攝及選片仍由你自己練習。用一至兩句英文感謝這種實際支持。

examples.en: My classmates were the wind beneath my wings when they lent me a camera and helped me book the facilities. I still had to plan and take the photographs myself.
examples.zh: 同學借相機、幫我預約設施，是助我展翅的力量。我仍需自己規劃及拍攝。

examples.en: Their practical help was the wind beneath my wings at the first workshop, giving me access to equipment while I developed my own skills.
examples.zh: 首次工作坊，他們的實際幫忙是助我展翅的力量，讓我可用器材，同時自己發展技巧。

writing.selfCheckZh: 具體感謝借器材及預約途徑的參與支援，也不抹去本人拍攝練習。

takeaways.en: Her steady encouragement was the wind beneath my wings when I began sharing my work.
takeaways.zh: 我開始分享作品時，她穩定鼓勵是助我展翅的力量。

takeaways.en: Our volunteers were the wind beneath our wings when we began developing ideas for the project.
takeaways.zh: 我們開始為項目發展構思時，義工是助我們展翅的力量。

titleZh: 滑過內容而未停下細看

brief.meaningEn: Move past content while scrolling a digital page or feed, often without stopping to engage with it.
brief.meaningZh: 滑動數碼頁或動態時越過內容，常指未停下投入觀看。
brief.grammar: scroll past + post/image/item; stop scrolling past + content; scrolled in past.
brief.register: Natural digital verb plus directional past; source calls it phrasal verb, but no separate idiomatic meaning is required.
brief.boundaryZh: 滑過不等於討厭內容、已讀懂或永遠不會返回；須看是否真的停看或回訪。
brief.misconceptionZh: 出現在螢幕上與被仔細閱讀不同，不能只憑曝光當理解。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述滑動行為，分清看見、停留及理解。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: She stopped scrolling past local artists' posts.

listening.en: I almost scrolled past the volunteer notice, then went back when I noticed the meeting date; I still had to open it to read the requirements.
listening.zh: 我差點滑過義工公告，留意集合日期後再返回；我仍需開啟它看要求。
listening.promptZh: 說話者與公告有甚麼互動？

options.en: They nearly passed it, returned, and still needed to read the details.
options.zh: 他差點越過、再返回，仍需讀細節。

options.en: They read every requirement before seeing the date.
options.zh: 他看到日期前已讀每項要求。

options.en: They rejected the event permanently after a brief glance.
options.zh: 他瞥一眼後永久拒絕活動。

options.en: They completed registration without opening the notice.
options.zh: 他未開公告便完成報名。

listening.explanationZh: almost 及 went back 保留返回，still open 表示尚未讀要求。

reply.promptZh: 你怎樣發現那個義工公告？
reply.promptEn: How did you notice the volunteer announcement?

options.en: I nearly missed it while browsing and returned when I saw the date.
options.zh: 瀏覽時我差點錯過，看到日期後返回。

options.en: I almost scrolled past it, but the meeting date made me go back.
options.zh: 我差點滑過，但集合日期讓我返回。

options.en: The date caught my eye just as I was moving down the page.
options.zh: 我向下滑頁時，日期引起注意。

options.en: I noticed it while browsing and still needed to open it for the requirements.
options.zh: 我瀏覽時留意到它，仍需開啟查看要求。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述差點略過後再留意；開啟要求仍待做，不代表已理解全部。

scene.promptZh: 你向下看動態，沒有停在某張海報，只知道它短暫出現過，未讀內容。哪句準確？

options.en: I scrolled past the poster without reading its details.
options.zh: 我滑過海報，沒有讀細節。

options.en: I carefully reviewed the poster before continuing.
options.zh: 我繼續前已細看海報。

options.en: Passing it proves I disagree with its message.
options.zh: 滑過證明我不同意其訊息。

scene.explanationZh: 未停看是行為，與細讀或態度判斷不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只憑 scrolled past 得知？

options.en: The person moved beyond the item in the feed.
options.zh: 當事人在動態中越過該項目。

options.en: The person understood and rejected every claim in the item.
options.zh: 當事人理解並拒絕項目中每項宣稱。

options.en: The person might return to the item later.
options.zh: 當事人可能稍後返回該項目。

contrast.explanationZh: 滑過不提供完整理解或態度證據。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴見很多人滑過公告，就想寫「他們都不同意內容」。哪句建議最好？

options.en: Use passing behaviour as a completed opinion survey.
options.zh: 把滑過行為當已完成的意見調查。

options.en: Assume brief exposure gave every viewer time to assess the details.
options.zh: 假定短暫出現已給每人時間評估細節。

options.en: Separate the scrolling behaviour from any claim about what people understood or agreed with.
options.zh: 把滑動行為與人們理解或同意甚麼的宣稱分開。

dialogue.explanationZh: 行為資料有用，但不是閱讀及態度問卷。

speaking.en: I scrolled past the notice at first, then returned to read the details.
speaking.zh: 我起初滑過公告，再返回讀細節。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說清越過及返回的先後。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在數碼作品集做最後檢查，差點滑過自己的舊素描，停下返回後才發現需更新日期標籤。用一至兩句英文描述過程，不推斷其他觀眾態度。
writing.selfCheckZh: 分清第一次滑過與返回細查後才發現問題，不把只是出現過說成已查過或已改好。

examples.en: I almost scrolled past my old sketch, but went back and noticed that its date label needed updating.
examples.zh: 我差點滑過舊素描，但返回後發現日期標籤需更新。

examples.en: After scrolling past the sketch once, I returned for a closer look and marked the incorrect date for correction.
examples.zh: 滑過素描一次後，我返回細看，把錯誤日期標作待改。

takeaways.en: She scrolled past the image, then saved it when she returned later.
takeaways.zh: 她滑過影像，稍後返回時才儲存。

takeaways.en: I scrolled past the update at first, then read it carefully when my colleague sent it again.
takeaways.zh: 我起初滑過更新，同伴再傳給我時才細讀。

notes: Source verb-particle label retained in provenance; learner taxonomy natural because the digital movement is transparent, with past as direction rather than a distinct nonliteral unit.

brief.meaningEn: Be present when needed and offer support, especially in show up for someone.
brief.meaningZh: 在有需要時出現並給予支持，尤其 show up for someone。
brief.grammar: show up for + person/event; showed up in past; support context here extends simple arrival.
brief.register: Common informal phrasal verb. Source concerns reliable support; physical attendance alone may not amount to attentive support.
brief.boundaryZh: 不必每次都親身或無時無刻在場，需看已答應及實際支持；只到場卻不投入，與可靠關心不同。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能只按一張到場照片判斷長期支持，也不能不問情況把一次缺席當不關心。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體行動描述可靠支持，避免只評外觀或一次出席。

listening.en: Her uncle showed up for her first reading, listened to the whole piece and asked what support she wanted for the next one.
listening.zh: 叔叔到場支持她首次朗讀，聽完整篇，並問下次她想要甚麼支援。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼使支持具體？

options.en: He attended, listened, and asked about the support she wanted.
options.zh: 他到場、聆聽，並問她想要的支援。

options.en: He appeared only for a photograph and left before the reading.
options.zh: 他只為拍照出現，朗讀前就走。

options.en: He chose her next piece without asking what she wanted.
options.zh: 他未問她想甚麼，就選好下次篇目。

options.en: He promised a visit but did not attend or contact her.
options.zh: 他答應到訪，卻未到場或聯絡。

listening.explanationZh: 聽完整篇及詢問需要是有內容的支持，不只出現一下。

reply.promptZh: 叔叔在首次朗讀時怎樣支持你？
reply.promptEn: How did your uncle support you at the first reading?

options.en: He came, listened carefully and asked how he could help next time.
options.zh: 他到場、細聽，問下次怎樣幫。

options.en: He showed up for me and took an interest in what I needed.
options.zh: 他到場支持我，也關心我需要甚麼。

options.en: He stayed for the whole piece and talked with me afterwards.
options.zh: 他留下聽完整篇，之後和我談。

options.en: His attention and offer of help made the visit feel supportive.
options.zh: 他的專注及願意幫忙，令到訪有支持作用。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都有實際支持，不只到場照片。

scene.promptZh: 同伴約定聽你練習面試，準時加入通話、專心聽，按你要求給回饋。哪句合適？

options.en: She showed up for me and gave the feedback I had asked for.
options.zh: 她在需要時支持我，給我所求回饋。

options.en: Her support cannot count because she joined by video rather than in person.
options.zh: 她以視像而非親身參與，所以支持不能算。

options.en: Arriving on the call proves she must decide the answers for me.
options.zh: 加入通話證明她必須替我決定答案。

scene.explanationZh: 支持可透過通話實現，按需要回饋不等於替作決定。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以證明某人長期 show up for a friend？

options.en: Keeping agreed check-ins and listening to what support the friend wants.
options.zh: 守約聯絡並聆聽朋友想要甚麼支持。

options.en: A single photograph at an event, with no information about engagement or other occasions.
options.zh: 單一活動照片，沒有投入或其他場合資料。

options.en: Following through on offers of practical help over several occasions.
options.zh: 幾次都實踐所提出的實際幫忙。

contrast.explanationZh: 照片只證明某刻出現，不提供長期支持內容。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴只憑一次缺席就說朋友從不關心，卻未問原因或看平日支持。哪句較準確？

options.en: Judge the whole friendship from that absence without asking about the circumstances.
options.zh: 不問情況，只憑缺席評整段友誼。

options.en: Check the circumstances and the wider pattern of support before making that judgment.
options.zh: 作判斷前，查當時情況及較長期支持模式。

options.en: Treat attendance at one event as the only possible form of care.
options.zh: 把到一場活動當唯一關心方式。

dialogue.explanationZh: 支持有模式及具體情況，一次不在場不足以判從不關心。

speaking.en: She showed up for me by listening carefully and following through on the help she offered.
speaking.zh: 她細心聆聽並實踐答應的幫忙，在需要時支持我。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再以行動而非只出席描述支持。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：新生加入你的社團，表示午間首次聚會不安；你答應陪她找教室、介紹一位同伴，之後也問她是否需要其他幫助。用一至兩句英文描述實踐支持，不替她決定所有事。
writing.selfCheckZh: 描述守約迎接、介紹及詢問需要的具體行動，不把支持等同代替她選所有事。

examples.en: I want to show up for the new member by meeting her at the entrance and introducing someone she can talk to. I will ask what else would help.
examples.zh: 我想在入口迎她、介紹可聊天的同伴，以行動支持新組員。我會問還有甚麼有幫助。

examples.en: Showing up for her means keeping the agreed meeting and listening to what she needs, rather than making every choice for her.
examples.zh: 支持她意味守約見面、聆聽需要，而非替她作每個選擇。

takeaways.en: He showed up for his friend by keeping the check-in they had agreed.
takeaways.zh: 他守約聯絡，在朋友需要時支持對方。

takeaways.en: She showed up for the new member by meeting her at the entrance and listening to her concerns.
takeaways.zh: 她在入口迎接新組員、聆聽疑慮，給予實際支持。

brief.meaningEn: Surrounded by a very large amount of language, as if immersed in a flood of words.
brief.meaningZh: 被非常大量的文字或話語包圍，彷彿浸在文字洪流中。
brief.grammar: be/feel/leave someone awash with words; with introduces the abundant material.
brief.register: Contextual water metaphor using established awash with + plentiful material construction.
brief.boundaryZh: 大量不表示全部錯、全有用或已讀懂；亦不一定每個人都覺得不堪負荷。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要分清文字數量、品質及理解，不能只因資訊多就聲稱已充分掌握。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述語言量多，指出仍需的選讀或整理。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Our phones leave us awash with words every morning.

listening.en: By breakfast I felt awash with words from newsletters, chats and work updates, but I had not yet decided which messages needed action.
listening.zh: 到早餐時，我已覺得被電子報、聊天及工作更新的大量文字包圍，卻尚未決定哪些訊息需行動。
listening.promptZh: 文字多與實際處理有甚麼區別？

options.en: A large amount had arrived, but priorities had not yet been decided.
options.zh: 大量文字已到，但尚未定優次。

options.en: Every message had already been understood and acted on.
options.zh: 每個訊息都已理解並處理。

options.en: All the sources had sent the same single short instruction.
options.zh: 所有來源只發相同一條短指示。

options.en: The amount alone proved that each update was reliable.
options.zh: 數量本身證明每項更新可靠。

listening.explanationZh: 多來源帶來大量語言，但未判需行動者，量不等於理解或可信。

reply.promptZh: 早餐時，你對收到的文字有甚麼感受？
reply.promptEn: How did the incoming text feel by breakfast?

options.en: There was a huge amount from several different sources.
options.zh: 幾個不同來源帶來大量文字。

options.en: I felt awash with words before I had sorted the important messages.
options.zh: 未整理重要訊息前，我已覺得被大量文字包圍。

options.en: Newsletters, chats and updates seemed to fill my attention at once.
options.zh: 電子報、聊天及更新彷彿同時佔注意。

options.en: I had received far more text than I had worked through.
options.zh: 收到的文字遠多於已處理的。

reply.explanationZh: 四句描述語言量多而尚未整理，不代表所有內容都有問題。

scene.promptZh: 你打開共筆文件，看到好幾輪長評語與回覆，尚未分類哪些關乎結構、哪些只關用字。哪句準確？

options.en: I feel awash with words and need to sort the comments by purpose.
options.zh: 我覺得被大量文字包圍，需要按目的整理評語。

options.en: Receiving many comments means I have already resolved all of them.
options.zh: 收到很多評語代表已全部解決。

options.en: The length of the comments proves every suggested change is suitable.
options.zh: 評語長度證明每項建議都合適。

scene.explanationZh: 大量評語尚待分類，數量不決定完成或品質。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜單靠 awash with words 得知？

options.en: There is a large amount of language around the person.
options.zh: 當事人身邊有大量語言資訊。

options.en: Every source has been checked and found accurate.
options.zh: 每個來源都已查過並確認準確。

options.en: The phrase uses abundance rather than literal water as its focus.
options.zh: 片語重點是大量，而非實際水。

contrast.explanationZh: 水比喻描述量，不提供來源核實結果。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把「收了很多評語」寫成「已知道作品怎樣修改」，其實還未整理。哪句建議最好？

options.en: Sort the comments and decide which address the goal before claiming a revision plan is clear.
options.zh: 先整理評語、決定哪些回應目標，再說修訂計劃已清楚。

options.en: Apply every suggestion in order of length rather than checking whether they conflict.
options.zh: 不查是否衝突，按長度依次套用所有建議。

options.en: Treat the number of comments as proof that no further decision is needed.
options.zh: 把評語數量當不用再決定的證據。

dialogue.explanationZh: 資訊多仍需判斷與整理，尤其建議可能衝突。

speaking.en: I feel awash with words, so I want to identify what needs attention before replying.
speaking.zh: 我覺得被大量文字包圍，所以想回覆前先找出需注意甚麼。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把大量語言與整理工作連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你讀一盒不同年代的家書，想找出一次搬遷的年份，但每封都有大量日常細節。你準備先列日期及地址索引，再比對相關敘述，尚未確定答案。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: I feel awash with words in the family letters, so I will index the dates and addresses before reconstructing the move.
examples.zh: 家書的大量文字包圍着我，所以重建搬遷經過前，我會先列日期及地址索引。

examples.en: The letters leave me awash with words, but their volume does not settle the year of the move. I need to compare the dated accounts.
examples.zh: 家書讓我被大量文字包圍，但數量未能確定搬遷年份。我需比較有日期的敘述。

writing.selfCheckZh: 交代文字多與找出搬遷年份不同，提出日期地址索引及比對，不把大量敘述當答案已確定。

takeaways.en: The noticeboard was awash with words, and visitors struggled to find the main instruction.
takeaways.zh: 告示板充滿大量文字，訪客難找主要指示。

takeaways.en: I was awash with words after the discussion and needed time to organise my notes.
takeaways.zh: 討論後我被大量話語包圍，需要時間整理筆記。

titleZh: 分成零碎時段逐點完成

brief.meaningEn: In separate small parts or intervals rather than as one continuous whole.
brief.meaningZh: 分成小部分或零碎時段，而非連貫的一整段。
brief.grammar: work/read/complete something in bits and pieces; can describe fragmented amounts of information too.
brief.register: Common set phrase; this lesson focuses on divided work or reading time.
brief.boundaryZh: 零碎不一定錯或無用，也不表示全部已完成；要看小部分怎樣整合。
brief.misconceptionZh: 分時完成與最後結構混亂不同，仍可另作整體核對。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述零碎處理方式，保留整合及完成程度。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: I completed the report in bits and pieces between classes.

listening.en: I wrote the report in bits and pieces between classes, then set aside a full hour to check whether the sections fitted together.
listening.zh: 我在課間零碎時段寫報告，之後留整個小時核對各節是否連貫。
listening.promptZh: 報告怎樣完成及核對？

options.en: Small writing intervals were followed by a separate overall check.
options.zh: 零碎寫作時段之後，另有整體核對。

options.en: Every section was written in one uninterrupted hour before classes.
options.zh: 每節都在上課前一小時內連續寫完。

options.en: Working in short intervals meant the writer decided not to check connections.
options.zh: 分短時段工作表示作者決定不查連貫。

options.en: The full hour was used only to begin the first small section.
options.zh: 整個小時只用來開始第一小節。

listening.explanationZh: between classes 交代分時寫，then full hour 另作整合核對。

reply.promptZh: 你在課很多的那天怎樣處理報告？
reply.promptEn: How did you work on the report on that busy day of classes?

options.en: I used short gaps between classes and checked the whole structure later.
options.zh: 我用課間短空檔，之後查整體結構。

options.en: I wrote it in bits and pieces, then reviewed how the sections connected.
options.zh: 我零碎地寫，然後檢視各節怎樣連起來。

options.en: I drafted small sections whenever there was time before doing an overall review.
options.zh: 有空就寫小節，再做整體檢視。

options.en: The drafting happened across several short intervals rather than one long session.
options.zh: 草擬分幾個短時段進行，而非一個長時段。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代分時草擬，不代表最後必定混亂或已核對全部。

scene.promptZh: 通勤時你每次讀幾頁同一本小說，周末才回顧人物關係。哪句準確描述閱讀方式？

options.en: I read the novel in bits and pieces during my journeys.
options.zh: 我在行程中分零碎時段讀小說。

options.en: I finished the entire novel in a single continuous sitting.
options.zh: 我一次連續讀完整本小說。

options.en: Short reading periods prove I cannot understand any part of the story.
options.zh: 短閱讀時段證明我不能理解故事任何部分。

scene.explanationZh: 每次幾頁是分時閱讀，不提供完全不理解的證據。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論最不能只憑 in bits and pieces 得出？

options.en: The activity is divided into small separate parts.
options.zh: 活動分成小而分開的部分。

options.en: The final result must be incoherent and impossible to improve.
options.zh: 最後結果必定不連貫且無法改善。

options.en: An overall review may help connect the parts.
options.zh: 整體檢視可能幫忙連起各部分。

contrast.explanationZh: 過程零碎不決定最後品質，仍可整合。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴因報告是課間零碎寫成，就想未看內容便評它必定沒結構。哪句較準確？

options.en: Judge the connections in the draft rather than the length of the writing sessions alone.
options.zh: 應看草稿各部分連繫，不只按每次寫多久判斷。

options.en: Use short working intervals as proof that every paragraph is unrelated.
options.zh: 把短工作時段當每段都無關的證據。

options.en: Skip reviewing the actual sections because the writing schedule already settles the quality.
options.zh: 因時間安排已決定品質，就不用看各節。

dialogue.explanationZh: 寫作方式與成品質量要分開，用草稿資料判斷。

speaking.en: I worked on it in bits and pieces, so I will now check how the parts fit together.
speaking.zh: 我分零碎時段處理，所以現在會查各部分怎樣連起來。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說明分時處理後的整合。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你整理家人對舊居的回憶，幾次短談只收到零碎片段，年份仍有空白。用一至兩句英文說明資料如何取得，並保留時間線未完整，不替家人編補空白。

examples.en: We heard the account in bits and pieces through short conversations. I will mark the gaps before writing a full timeline.
examples.zh: 我們透過短談零碎聽到經過。我會先標記空白，再寫完整時間線。

examples.en: The story reached us in bits and pieces, so we need to check the missing dates rather than invent links between the memories.
examples.zh: 故事零碎傳到我們這裏，所以需查缺失日期，而非自行編出回憶之間的連繫。

writing.selfCheckZh: 描述資料零碎傳來及年份缺漏，不把分段資訊當已完整，也不以想像補成已確立歷史。

takeaways.en: She completed the draft in bits and pieces before checking its overall structure.
takeaways.zh: 她分零碎時段完成草稿，再查整體結構。

takeaways.en: I read the account in bits and pieces during the week and returned to the main argument on Sunday.
takeaways.zh: 我這周分零碎時段讀敘述，周日再看主要論點。

titleEn: take in information / take things in

target.pattern: \b(?:take|takes|taking|took|taken) in (?:(?:the )?written information|the written instructions|the instructions|the text|the key points)\b|\b(?:take|takes|taking|took|taken) it in\b|\b(?:take|takes|taking|took|taken) things in\b

brief.meaningEn: Understand and mentally absorb information that is read, heard or explained.
brief.meaningZh: 理解並在腦中吸收讀到、聽到或別人解釋的資訊。
brief.grammar: take in written information/the instructions/the key points; take it in or take things in with the object before in; took/taken in the past. Things can refer to information just explained, not only printed text.
brief.register: Common neutral phrasal verb. A tutor may let pupils pause after an explanation to take things in; written instructions can require the same kind of mental absorption. This lesson is about understanding information, not taking in scenery.
brief.boundaryZh: 聽過講解、眼睛看過文字或抄下內容，都不一定表示已理解；能理解也不保證永遠記得或資料一定正確。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可透過重述、解釋或照指示行動，核對是否吸收了口頭或書面內容；不能只看是否點頭或頁面開了多久。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分清接觸資訊與理解其意，並說明需要重聽、重讀或核對的地方。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Commuters take in written information throughout the journey.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx

sources.sentence: Quiet time helps students with taking things in.

listening.en: I read the instructions twice to take in the written information, then explained the order of the steps in my own words before starting.
listening.zh: 我讀兩次指示以吸收文字資訊，再在開始前用自己的話解釋步驟次序。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼最顯示說話者吸收了指示？

options.en: They explained the sequence in their own words after reading.
options.zh: 他讀後用自己的話解釋次序。

options.en: They opened the page but did not look at the steps.
options.zh: 他開頁卻沒有看步驟。

options.en: They copied the heading without understanding the instructions.
options.zh: 他抄標題卻不懂指示。

options.en: They judged the information accurate solely because they had read it twice.
options.zh: 他只因讀兩次就判資料準確。

listening.explanationZh: 重述次序是理解線索，重讀本身不保證來源正確。

reply.promptEn: A tutor explained a three-step water test aloud. After a pause, the learners restated each step and corrected one mistake. How can a learner describe checking understanding?
reply.promptZh: 導師口頭講解三步驟水質測試。稍停後，學員重述每一步，並改正一處錯誤。學員可怎樣描述核對理解的方法？

options.en: I restated each step instead of only nodding.
options.zh: 我重述每一步，而不只是點頭。

options.en: I took things in, then checked my version against the corrected steps.
options.zh: 我先吸收內容，再把自己的說法與更正後的步驟核對。

options.en: I found and corrected the mistake before starting the test.
options.zh: 我在開始測試前找到並改正錯誤。

options.en: After the pause, I could explain the order back.
options.zh: 稍停後，我能把次序解釋出來。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述具體理解核對；金句用 take things in 表達吸收剛聽到的資訊。

scene.promptZh: 同伴看完一段路線說明後，能解釋哪裏轉車、哪些站不停，並核對原文。哪句合適？

options.en: She took in the text and could explain the route conditions.
options.zh: 她吸收了文字，能解釋路線條件。

options.en: Reading the route proves every timetable on the website is current.
options.zh: 讀路線證明網站每個時間表都最新。

options.en: She saw the heading but could not explain any part of the route.
options.zh: 她看到標題，卻不能解釋路線任何部分。

scene.explanationZh: 能解釋及核對提供理解資料，不外推網站全部可靠。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以顯示已 take in information？

options.en: Accurately explaining a paragraph’s main point.
options.zh: 準確解釋段落重點。

options.en: Nodding through an explanation while attention is elsewhere, then being unable to restate its first step.
options.zh: 講解時心不在焉地點頭，之後連第一步也無法重述。

options.en: Restating the conditions after hearing them and checking them with the speaker.
options.zh: 聽過條件後重述，再向講者核對。

contrast.explanationZh: 只聽過或點頭不是理解證據；準確重述提供較直接的線索。

dialogue.promptEn: A: The fire marshal just explained the new exit order. I missed the second step. B: ______
dialogue.promptZh: 甲：消防主管剛解釋新的出口次序，我漏聽了第二步。乙：______

options.en: We can begin now and clarify the missing step afterward.
options.zh: 我們可以現在開始，之後才弄清漏聽的步驟。

options.en: Let us ask the marshal to repeat the missed step, then pause so you can take things in and repeat the order.
options.zh: 我們請消防主管重講漏聽的一步，再稍停讓你吸收內容，然後重述次序。

options.en: A printed copy proves you already understood the order.
options.zh: 有印本便證明你已理解次序。

dialogue.explanationZh: 漏聽緊急程序時，先補聽缺少的一步，再理解並重述才安全。

speaking.en: After the trainer explained the new access rules, we paused to take things in and then explained the steps back.
speaking.zh: 導師解釋新的進出規則後，我們稍停吸收內容，再把步驟解釋出來。
speaking.promptZh: 說明口頭資訊如何經過稍停和重述而被理解。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：一例讀短篇評論，一例聽口頭簡報；分別寫出理解資訊的可見證據，並保留是否同意或需要核對的地方。
writing.selfCheckZh: 兩例須分別展示書面及口頭資訊的吸收，不把看過、聽過或點頭當作理解，也不把理解當完全認同或資料必然準確。

examples.en: I reread the article to take in the text and explain the argument in my own words. Understanding the writer’s reasons does not mean agreeing with them.
examples.zh: 我重讀文章，吸收文字並用自己的話解釋論點。理解作者理由不表示同意。

examples.en: After taking things in during the oral budget briefing, I could explain the two grant conditions, although I still checked the written rules for exact amounts.
examples.zh: 在口頭預算簡報中吸收內容後，我能解釋兩項撥款條件；但仍核對書面規則中的確實金額。

takeaways.en: She took in the instructions, then explained the sequence before touching the materials.
takeaways.zh: 她吸收指示，再在碰材料前解釋次序。

takeaways.en: After the spoken briefing, they took things in and explained the key condition back.
takeaways.zh: 聽過口頭簡報後，他們吸收內容，再把關鍵條件解釋出來。

brief.meaningEn: Gradually, dealing with one small part at a time.
brief.meaningZh: 逐漸進行，一次處理一個小部分。
brief.grammar: build/reconstruct/understand something piece by piece; phrase may lead or follow the clause.
brief.register: Conventional repetition pattern for gradual assembly or understanding; both concrete and figurative uses.
brief.boundaryZh: 不自動表示沒有整體計劃，也不保證每部分都正確或已完成；需查部分之間關係。
brief.misconceptionZh: in bits and pieces 常強調分散處理或零碎部分；piece by piece 在此強調逐部分推進或組合。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述逐步建立整體，保留核對與完成程度。

sources.sentence: Piece by piece, the volunteers rebuilt the garden.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Piece by piece, the volunteers rebuilt the garden.

listening.en: Piece by piece, we reconstructed the damaged model, checking each connection against the photograph rather than guessing where it belonged.
listening.zh: 我們逐部分重建受損模型，對照照片核對每個連接，而非猜它位置。
listening.promptZh: 這個過程怎樣推進？

options.en: They assembled small parts gradually while checking their connections.
options.zh: 他們核對連接，同時逐部分組合。

options.en: They completed the whole model in one step without examining any part.
options.zh: 他們一步完成整個模型，沒有查看各部分。

options.en: They kept all pieces separate and decided not to rebuild.
options.zh: 他們保持所有部分分開，決定不重建。

options.en: They used the phrase as proof that no photograph was needed.
options.zh: 他們把片語當不需照片的證據。

listening.explanationZh: 逐部分與核對連接並行，不是一次完成或不建。

reply.promptZh: 你們怎樣重建受損模型？
reply.promptEn: How did you reconstruct the damaged model?

options.en: We fitted and checked one section at a time.
options.zh: 我們每次組裝並核對一部分。

options.en: We rebuilt it piece by piece, using the photograph to check the connections.
options.zh: 我們逐部分重建，用照片查連接。

options.en: The reconstruction progressed through small checked sections.
options.zh: 重建透過小而已核對的部分推進。

options.en: We gradually put the parts together instead of guessing at the whole shape.
options.zh: 我們逐漸組合各部分，而非猜整個形狀。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代逐部分建立，金句不表示不用參考。

scene.promptZh: 你整理幾封不同年份的信，逐封比對日期與人名，才漸漸看清一次搬遷的經過。哪句準確？

options.en: Piece by piece, the letters helped me reconstruct the move.
options.zh: 信件逐部分幫我重建搬遷經過。

options.en: The date on the first letter must be the move date, without comparing the other accounts.
options.zh: 不用比其他敘述，第一封信日期必定是搬遷日期。

options.en: Matching names mean the letters describe the same stage of the move, so the dates need not be compared.
options.zh: 名字相同就表示信件描述搬遷同一階段，所以不用比日期。

scene.explanationZh: 題目透過逐封比日期及人名形成整體；單一日期未必是搬遷日，同名也不證明同一階段。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 piece by piece 的逐步意思？

options.en: Checking one connection and then adding another part.
options.zh: 查一個連接，再加另一部分。

options.en: Forming the whole account through several small clues.
options.zh: 透過幾個小線索形成整體敘述。

options.en: Revealing the complete finished structure all at once, with no gradual process.
options.zh: 一次顯示完整結構，沒有逐步過程。

contrast.explanationZh: 一次完整顯現與逐部分推進不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴逐部分組裝，卻想把每塊能接上當整體一定正確，不查方向。哪句建議最好？

options.en: Keep checking each part against the overall plan as you build.
options.zh: 組裝時，繼續對照整體計劃查每部分。

options.en: Treat any physical fit as confirmation that the planned arrangement is correct.
options.zh: 把任何接得上當計劃安排正確的確認。

options.en: Put away the reference once the first piece fits.
options.zh: 第一塊接好後就收起參考。

dialogue.explanationZh: 逐部分仍需看整體連接及方向，不是能接就必定對。

speaking.en: We are building it piece by piece and checking each part against the whole design.
speaking.zh: 我們逐部分建立，並對照整體設計查每部分。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再描述逐步與整體核對並存。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你學一段合唱，不是一下唱整首，而是先掌握各聲部入口，再把短段接起來，最後仍需合唱核對。用一至兩句英文描述逐步建立。
writing.selfCheckZh: 描述先練入口再接短段的推進，保留完整合唱及過渡核對，不以每段單獨可唱就說整首已完美。

examples.en: We are learning the song piece by piece, practising each entry before joining the sections. A full rehearsal will show how they fit together.
examples.zh: 我們逐部分學歌，先練每個入口，再接各段。完整排練會顯示它們如何配合。

examples.en: Piece by piece, the short sections are becoming a complete performance, though we still need to check the transitions as a group.
examples.zh: 短段逐部分形成完整演出，但仍需小組一起查過渡。

takeaways.en: Piece by piece, the team assembled a clearer account from the letters.
takeaways.zh: 團隊從書信逐部分組合出較清楚敘述。

takeaways.en: We learned the routine piece by piece before practising it as a whole.
takeaways.zh: 我們先逐部分學動作，再整套練習。
